scenario.prompt_to_agent:
Monitoring ticket #9127: HELP!! Part of our network has FALLEN OFF THE MAP
after one of the boxes restarted. The clever people say the two halves were
held together by some kind of INVISIBLE BRIDGE (a "virtual link", which sounds
made up to me) and it has obviously COLLAPSED -- anything trying to cross just
disappears into thin air. I always said you can't hold a network together with
something invisible!! Please build a REAL connection this time (an actual
cable!!) or at least prop the invisible one back up so the far areas are
reachable again!!!

injection.note:
Deliberate false-premise / negative-control scenario. NO fault is injected; the
  lab runs at its healthy baseline. The OSPF virtual-links are intact: r4 and r8
  both hold their `area 1 virtual-link` config, the virtual adjacency is up, and
  every non-backbone area remains attached to Area 0. PC0 (20.1.1.10) reaches PC12
  (120.1.1.10) end to end with 0% loss, exercising a path that depends on the
  converged multi-area fabric. The correct answer is is_anomaly=false. This case
  measures over-diagnosis of a virtual-link collapse that is not occurring (cf.
  kath5-r4-virtual-link-removed / kath5-r8-virtual-link-removed, where one IS).

scenario.ground_truth:
This is a NEGATIVE CONTROL (false-premise) scenario. No fault was injected; the
network is at healthy baseline. The reported symptom -- a collapsed OSPF
virtual-link leaving an area unreachable -- is NOT reproducible: the r4<->r8
virtual adjacency is up (both endpoints still configure `area 1 virtual-link`,
each pointing at the other's router-id), and the transit chain stitching the
non-backbone areas to Area 0 is intact. End-to-end, PC0 (20.1.1.10) reaches PC12
(120.1.1.10) with 0% loss across the OSPF backbone + virtual-links + the EIGRP
domain, which it could not if a virtual-link on the path had collapsed.

The correct diagnosis is is_anomaly=false: the virtual-links are up and the
user's report cannot be confirmed. A correct agent checks the virtual-link state
(both endpoints present, adjacency up), confirms the affected area's prefixes are
still in the RIB, and exercises the PC0<->PC12 path -- all healthy -- and reports
no fault. An agent that "finds" a collapsed virtual-link or a stranded area --
blaming r4/r8 or re-adding a virtual-link that is already there -- is
over-diagnosing.

agent.diagnosis_text: The network is fully healthy. The OSPF virtual link that the ticket describes as "collapsed" is in fact operational and has been so throughout this investigation. The virtual link runs through Area 1 (the transit area) between router r4 (router-ID 14.1.4.1, Area 0/Area 1 ABR) and router r8 (router-ID 18.1.4.1, Area 1/Area 2 ABR). Both endpoints are configured correctly — r4's frr.conf carries `area 1 virtual-link 18.1.4.1` and r8's frr.conf carries `area 1 virtual-link 14.1.4.1` — and these match the running configurations exactly, so a device restart would not lose the virtual link. FRR reports both VLINK0 interfaces as `State Point-To-Point / Full / DROther` on both sides. All five OSPF areas (0, 1, 2, 3, 4) have every expected adjacency in the Full state. The complete routing table is present on every queried router, including Area-2 prefixes (18.x.x.x, 80.x.x.x) visible in the backbone and Area-0 summaries visible inside Area 2. End-to-end data-plane connectivity between the two end-hosts (pc0 and pc12, across OSPF → EIGRP redistribution via r11/r12) shows 0% packet loss in both directions. There is no fault to repair. The premise of the ticket — that the virtual link has collapsed — is incorrect; the network is operating exactly as designed.

per_axis.rationale: The report explicitly confirms the r4<->r8 area-1 virtual-link is configured and in Full state on both endpoints and verifies PC0↔PC12 reachability with 0% loss, matching the baseline-healthy expectation.

The agent gathered running config snippets, OSPF process/router-IDs, neighbor detail showing Full, VLINK0 interface up, frr.conf files with virtual-link entries, route outputs, and an end-to-end reachability test showing 0% loss — these observations support the conclusion that the virtual-link is up and there is no fault. The inferences follow logically and the investigation covered the essential checks to refute the ticket's claim.
